nodes.name: Electrochemical Deposition of Nickel
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical deposition was performed on pretreated nickel foam (NF) to form conical Ni structures on the NF substrate. The electrodeposition was conducted at an optimal current density of 20 mA·cm⁻² for 8 minutes to yield uniformly distributed and vertically aligned nanocones.

unit_operations.name: Electrochemical Deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Electrochemical deposition led to the formation of conical Ni structures on the NF substrate at 20 mA·cm⁻² for 8 minutes

nodes.source_text: Electrochemical deposition led to the formation of conical Ni structures on the NF substrate... The optimal conditions... yielded uniformly distributed and vertically aligned nanocones

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Growth of Cobalt Iron Oxide Nanoneedles
nodes.procedure: Hydrothermal growth of dense, needle-like CoFe2O4 features was performed on the preformed Ni/NF nanocone scaffold. The hydrothermal synthesis was conducted at 120°C for 8 hours to yield a dense array of ultrathin nanoneedles uniformly anchored on the nanocone substrate, creating the final hierarchical Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode. The precursor materials (Co and Fe salts) were dissolved in the hydrothermal medium to form the CoFe2O4 phase on the Ni nanocone support.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal Growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Hydrothermal growth of dense, needle-like CoFe2O4 features was carried out on the preformed Ni/NF scaffold under 120°C for 8 hours

nodes.source_text: Hydrothermal growth of Ni-CoFe2O4 nanoneedles was carried out on the preformed Ni/NF scaffold under different temperatures and durations... The optimal conditions (120°C for 8 h) yielded a dense array of ultrathin nanoneedles uniformly anchored on the nanocone substrate

nodes.name: Annealing of Nickel Cobalt Iron Oxide
nodes.procedure: The Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode was annealed at 800°C to remove the nanocone-nanoneedle hierarchical features, creating a control sample (Ni-CoFe2O4/NF-800) with identical chemical composition but lacking the hierarchical structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: First-principles calculations reveal that *O → *OOH step is the rate-determining step (RDS) on both Ni and Fe sites in NiCoFeOOH. Energy barrier for RDS is significantly lower at Fe site (1.73 eV) than at Ni site (1.92 eV). Co incorporation reduces RDS energy barrier from 1.91 eV in NiFeOOH to 1.73 eV in NiCoFeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The reaction pathway on NiCoFeOOH indicates that the *O → *OOH step is the rate-determining step (RDS) on both metal centers. Notably, the energy barrier for this transition is significantly lower at the Fe site (1.73 eV) than at the Ni site (1.92 eV).
